candidates.title: Document and navigate schematic designs

demandEvidence.chore: Document schematic designs and make their contents easier for electrical engineers to navigate.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Documentation tool for EEs to document and navigate their designs better.

ease.reason: A student can make an annotated index from supplied excerpts, but no source supports PDF analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: engineering teams may pay to find design details faster; the post establishes no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can organize a small supplied sample; extraction accuracy remains unverified.

autonomy.reason: A person must supply and verify schematic details; no implementation capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The post describes documentation and navigation for engineers, but gives no workflow, frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: A useful output depends on unsupported schematic interpretation; the provisional mean is below six.

experimentPlan.output: A one-page index of supplied schematic sections with plain-language labels and page references.
inputs: Synthetic schematic excerpts with page numbers
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a small sample for indexing.
steps: Draft an index with page references.
Have an engineer verify every entry.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check each entry against its supplied page reference and confirm no unsupported component claim was added.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An engineer supplies permitted materials and approves labels before sharing.

candidates.title: Consolidate scattered trip details

demandEvidence.chore: Collect trip details scattered across spreadsheets, airline apps, old inboxes and a photo library into one place.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: My trips were scattered across a spreadsheet, airline apps, old inboxes and a photo library, so I built Trvlrr to hold all of it.

ease.reason: A beginner can organize sample itinerary text, but no source documents extraction or automation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: frequent travelers or travel assistants might pay; this post records no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can organize a sample packet; source variety and accuracy remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A traveler must verify every booking fact; no automated workflow is documented.

evidence.reason: The post names four scattered sources and says its author built a place to hold them; outcomes are absent.

candidates.reason: A narrow trip brief is scopeable, but extraction and source access are undocumented; mean below six.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed trip brief listing supplied dates, destinations and booking references.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies one fictional trip packet.
steps: Group details by date and destination.
Draft a brief with source references.
Have the operator verify every booking fact.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Compare each brief entry with the sample and confirm dates and references match.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A traveler supplies permitted inputs and checks every booking detail.
unverified: Extraction across email, spreadsheets and images

candidates.title: Draft booking and service notifications

demandEvidence.chore: Draft booking confirmations, provider assignment notices, payment-status updates and customer alerts for an on-demand service application.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How can n8n help automate booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts?

ease.reason: A beginner can draft notices from fictional events, but integrations are unsupported.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: on-demand service operators may pay for dependable updates; no buying intent is established.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can map events to drafts; APIs, concurrency and payment accuracy are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The loop is repeatable, but a person must verify payment status and approve each message.

evidence.reason: The post names confirmations, assignment, payment updates, alerts, retries and duplicate prevention, but no schema or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete chores support a bounded mock, but execution lacks implementation evidence; mean below six.

experimentPlan.output: A draft booking confirmation or provider assignment notice from a fictional event.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a test with one fictional booking event.
steps: Have a person approve or discard the draft.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check every name, status and time against the input and confirm missing fields are flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies templates and reviews every draft; no live message is sent.

candidates.title: Route sample email by text rules

demandEvidence.chore: Sort incoming emails by operator-defined text using conditional routing.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Additionally, the IF Node doesn’t output the Boolean value (true or false) as expected, so the emails aren’t being sorted correctly.

ease.reason: A beginner can test synthetic text conditions; n8n documents conditional comparison routes, not email integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small firms might pay for inbox sorting; this troubleshooting post shows no buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic test is feasible; the If reference supports conditional splits only, not Code Node repair.

autonomy.reason: Conditional comparisons can route samples, but a person must select terms and authorize live changes.

evidence.reason: The post describes text recognition and routing failures; the reference confirms comparisons, not a working solution.

candidates.reason: The reference supports conditional routing only; the specific Code Node issue remains unsupported and mean below six.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed routing table showing which synthetic email matches each operator-defined rule.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies samples and expected categories.
steps: Compare proposed routes with expected labels.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Verify every route against expected labels and count mismatches.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator defines categories, supplies fictional messages and approves live edits.
unverified: Live inbox access and privacy review

candidates.title: Share Messenger text and image context

demandEvidence.chore: Pass an already-received image and accompanying text together to one agent to avoid asking the customer to resend the image.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: The problem occurs when a customer sends an image along with a message such as, “I want this product.”

ease.reason: A student can test linked synthetic inputs, but no source supports Messenger routing or image analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: service businesses handling image inquiries may pay; this post proves no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A mock can test combined inputs, but live image access and recognition are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A human must verify image interpretation and approve replies; integration is undocumented.

evidence.reason: The post describes text and image routes and the repeated-image problem, but no recurrence or outcome.

candidates.reason: The specific context-passing problem lacks support for image or Messenger capabilities; mean below six.

experimentPlan.output: A draft response context pairing a fictional message with an operator-written image description.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a test with one synthetic text-and-image pair.
steps: Record text and image description together.
Check both appear in the combined input.
Have a person verify and approve any reply.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Confirm the output includes the supplied description and adds no absent product facts.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies or describes the test image, reviews and approves any reply.

candidates.title: Triage a reported automation failure

demandEvidence.chore: Review a specific automation failure using expected and actual results and prepare a focused troubleshooting note.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Webhooks receiving data but not updating the correct records

ease.reason: A student can structure an issue report; Make documents error handlers, not sync diagnosis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small firms with broken scenarios may pay; the post offers fixed-price help but records no sale.

feasibility.reason: A sample intake can capture expected and actual behavior; live diagnosis remains unverified.

autonomy.reason: An intake loop can organize symptoms, but a technician must inspect and verify fixes.

evidence.reason: The post lists webhook and sync faults and offers fixed-price review; no case result is shown.

candidates.reason: Concrete fault categories and a service offer appear, but Make documentation covers error routes only; mean below six.

experimentPlan.output: A troubleshooting note separating the reported symptom, expected result, actual result and next evidence to collect.
experimentPlan.trigger: A technician enters one specific failure report.
steps: Identify the supplied integration or step.
List supplied module errors for human inspection.
Have a technician verify before any suggestion.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Confirm every statement maps to supplied details and no root cause is asserted without evidence.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A technician supplies authorized redacted details and reviews all questions and changes.
unverified: Access to real scenarios and logs

candidates.title: Compare supplied AWS scaling options

demandEvidence.chore: Compare operator-supplied cost options for a bootstrapped startup seeking to scale on AWS affordably.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: If you are a bootstrapped startup and need to scale on AWS but can't afford it

ease.reason: A beginner can format supplied options; no source supports AWS cost or architecture analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: bootstrapped startups may pay for scaling advice; no paying AI customer is established.

feasibility.reason: A mock can organize supplied options and constraints; no verification method is given.

autonomy.reason: A person must verify costs and infrastructure effects; automated analysis is undocumented.

evidence.reason: The post offers help to startups seeking affordable AWS scaling without workflow or cost details.

candidates.reason: The post identifies affordability but gives no task inputs or verification method; mean below six.

experimentPlan.output: A comparison memo listing operator-supplied AWS options, costs and stated trade-offs.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies options and a goal for a mock comparison.
steps: Record each supplied option and estimate.
List the stated goal and constraints.
Have a specialist verify before use.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Recalculate totals and label each trade-off as supplied or unverified.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A specialist supplies and verifies figures; no production change is made.
